papers.title: DarkMatterFM-Registry: A Machine-Readable Registry of Dark-Matter Models Extracted from the arXiv Literature
papers.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences Workshop (ML4PS), NeurIPS 2026. Registry, schemas, and code: https://ioanazelko.github.io/darkmatterfm-registry/
papers.summary: An LLM pipeline extracts 6,145 dark-matter model cards from arXiv full texts, validates schemas, and maps high-priority infrastructure gaps.
papers.tldr: It is found that what blocks the most high-priority models is not missing theory but missing shared infrastructure: model files for existing relic-abundance solvers, a general non-cold Boltzmann-code framework, reusable indirect-detection likelihoods, and a Lyman-$\alpha$ forest likelihood for non-cold dark matter (the largest gap for structure-formation probes).

papers.title: A pipeline for identifying astrophysical signals and instrumental glitches in LISA data
papers.summary: A search plus machine-learning classifier distinguishes gravitational-wave transients from instrumental glitches in simulated LISA data with about 98% accuracy and fast processing.

papers.title: New optimisations for exact, scalable 2D Gaussian process inference, with applications to astronomical time-series
papers.summary: New exact Kronecker-product Gaussian process inference in JAX enables scalable 2D modelling of correlated noise in JWST exoplanet spectroscopy and other astronomical time-series.
